races.name: MJG Group Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Pull The Rug
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Grace Harris who has modest form at 6f on good ground (one win from eight similar-going runs) and is making only limited appeal in a race shape likely to reward those closer to a contested pace.

runners_data.name: Bold Shout
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's three-year-old won over 6f on good ground and has placed on soft, sitting just off the speed from draw 5; the 2/20 trainer 14-day strike rate is solid and he is the most obvious danger to the Strand top pick from a prominent berth.

runners_data.name: Black Endeavour
runners_data.note: Callum Rodriguez rides a horse whose best recent form — a 6f win on Good to Soft — aligns with today's conditions, and though he maps to midfield he has previously raced prominently; tongue-tie applied and only 8 days since last run are factors to note.

runners_data.name: Maid In Devon
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's progressive filly has won three of her last five including at 6f on soft going and on Good to Soft; Lewis Edmunds takes over from draw 10 on a horse who can dominate from the front, and the going report confirming Good to Soft for this race suits her profile precisely.

runners_data.name: Jenny Jerome
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly whose best recent effort was a placed run over 5f on soft but who has struggled over 6f in three attempts at that trip, and William Carver faces a task from a horse with only one placing in five recent outings.

runners_data.name: Red Snapper
runners_data.note: Kathy Turner's filly has won her last two starts over 6f on good ground and wears a hood; Ben Ffrench Davis (5lb claim) rides a genuine hold-up type who will need the pace to be truly brutal to land a blow from the rear, though her recent form is the best in the race.

runners_data.name: Nebbia
runners_data.note: Hughie Morrison's hold-up specialist has form figures of 8-8 over distances longer than today's 6f and is genuinely racing out of her comfort zone in terms of both trip and running style; although mapped to midfield for redistribution purposes, she is a true rear-runner who will likely find this race shape and distance difficult.

runners_data.name: Eightthreeone
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's front-runner has a 3/34 trainer 14-day record and a willing but win-less recent sequence at 6f; she will press Maid In Devon hard early from draw 6 but her pattern suggests she is more likely to set the table for others than win herself.

runners_data.name: White Ladder
runners_data.note: 60 days since last run is a query for John Ryan's hold-up type who placed on soft over 7f but has not won; Callum Shepherd rides a horse who is better over a longer trip and will need something to go wrong further forward.

runners_data.name: Mollstar
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's prominent racer (6/42 trainer 14-day, very active yard) placed over 6f on good ground last time; draw 4 gives him a chance to slot in handy but his form figures suggest he finds it hard to win rather than place.

runners_data.name: Guernsey Angel
runners_data.note: Pat Cosgrave picks up the ride for David Evans on a prominent type who has finished second over 6f on Good to Soft but whose overall record at this course and trip is modest; draw 12 is wide and she may struggle to dominate from that position.

runners_data.name: Pilgrim's Progress
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's prominent runner has placed at 5f and 6f on similar ground but has not won; Alec Voikhansky takes the ride and the horse profiles as a reliable but not dominant presence in a race with more prominent types than can all get their position.

runners_data.name: Madman
runners_data.note: Jack Callan's prominent racer has won twice at 6f on good ground and placed on soft, arriving here on a career-best OR of 70; his recent form (wins at 6f and a second on soft) is among the strongest in the field and he is the chief danger if the front two burn each other out.

races.paceDynamic: Maid In Devon and Eightthreeone are the two confirmed front-runners in a 13-runner field, and with four prominent-style horses (Bold Shout, Mollstar, Guernsey Angel, Pilgrim's Progress, Madman) also seeking early positions, the early gallop will be genuinely contested rather than sedate — on Good to Soft ground at Salisbury, that translates to an honest, sustained tempo from the off. Maid In Devon has won three of her last five at this trip and on this surface profile and is the more natural, dominant pace-setter; Eightthreeone will push her but has failed to win from the front in her last four starts, suggesting Maid In Devon is the likelier pace controller. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their preferred positions — Nebbia, a genuine hold-up operator pushed to the map's midfield for redistribution purposes, is the clearest example, while Madman and Pilgrim's Progress may find themselves shuffled back further than ideal. This race shape — a genuinely contested but not suicidal pace on a fair Salisbury 6f in soft-ish conditions — strongly favours a horse with tactical versatility or the ability to track just off the speed and pick up, and Maid In Devon's proven ability to control from the front on similar going makes her the dominant beneficiary if the pace is honest rather than frenetic.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Maid In Devon Controls Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Maid In Devon establishes a clear early lead and dictates a strong but sustainable gallop that stretches the field.
scenarios.body: Maid In Devon has won on soft ground over 6f and shows a pattern of front-running wins at this trip; a genuine pace here paradoxically suits her because she has the fitness and experience to handle pressure before asserting.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the dual front-runners burn each other off and a close-to-pace runner swoops in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Madman arrives from a prominent position with his strong recent form (wins at 66 and 69 OR level) and handles soft well; Bold Shout also profiles as a horse who can sit just off the pace and finish with purpose on Good to Soft.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closer Storms Home
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely fierce and the race completely collapses for the front two inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Red Snapper has back-to-back 6f wins and can close from off the pace; White Ladder placed over soft ground at 7f and would relish survivors of an attrition race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Two Collapse, Midfield Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If both front-runners over-race and the pace implodes, allowing a prominent-to-midfield type to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: Black Endeavour's recent win over 6f on Good to Soft and ability to race from midfield gives him a profile that suits a messy shape; Guernsey Angel has placed at this trip and can produce a one-paced but consistent effort.

watchPoints.text: Maid In Devon and Eightthreeone are both confirmed front-runners — watch how quickly they establish positions in the first furlong, as a fierce duel between them rather than one controlling could compromise both their chances and open the race up dramatically.

Madman arrives on the back of two wins and a place on soft going with an OR of 70 — if he gets a prominent pitch from draw 13 and the pace is honest, he represents the most significant threat to the Strand top pick.

Bold Shout is drawn 5 in a handy position and has the profile of a horse who can race just off the pace on Good to Soft; Hector Crouch is an in-form jockey and this combination could easily land the places if not the win.

Nebbia is a genuine hold-up type redistributed to midfield on the map — discount any scenario that relies on her getting a prominent position, as in a field this competitive she will almost certainly be further back than ideal for her chance.

Red Snapper's back-to-back 6f wins are the most recent winning form in the race but she is a hold-up type relying on a truly run race; if the pace is honest rather than suicidal, she is a place contender rather than a win contender.

races.name: PKF Francis Clark Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Tenbob Tommy
runners_data.note: Won twice on good ground over 6f recently but his sole soft-going start produced a poor effort; prominent racer from draw 2 who will look to slot in behind Padua early, though the going is a legitimate query.

runners_data.name: Sergeant Pep
runners_data.note: Clive Cox in good form (2/20 14-day), Rossa Ryan booked — finished third last time on soft, second and third before that, so this ground suits; prominent style from draw 7 means he'll need to travel across to get a clean position, but he's the most consistent in this field.

runners_data.name: Supreme King
runners_data.note: Strand's top selection at low confidence; hold-up runner whose best form has come on good ground, though he has two soft starts in recent history; Pat Cosgrave's patient approach from draw 8 plays to the scenario where the prominent group tires late.

runners_data.name: Rare Change
runners_data.note: Won on soft over 7f and wears a hood; hold-up horse whose recent form has been littered with mid-division finishes on going faster than today, so this softer surface could unlock him — Jack Callan will need to find daylight at the business end.

runners_data.name: The Quiet Gent
runners_data.note: 35 days since last run is worth noting; another hold-up type with a tongue-tie who has placed on good ground twice but hasn't run on soft in these five runs — draw 6 is workable but he needs the pace to materialise.

runners_data.name: Baldomero
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran fitted with a hood; prominent racer who drew badly wide last time and struggled, but placed on good ground at 6f in this yard's care; Michael Appleby's 3/26 14-day stat is respectable, though age counts slightly against.

runners_data.name: Padua
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner — tongue-tie worn, 24 days fresh, and stepping back to 6f after two runs at 7f; his single soft-going start produced a beaten effort at 11 lengths, though on a flat track setting his own fractions, he's a significant pace asset regardless.

runners_data.name: Safari Dream
runners_data.note: In hot form with two recent wins on good ground; drawn wide at 9, which makes him a backmarker on paper despite a prominent style — Lewis Edmunds will need to decide early whether to bowl forward or accept a tighter position, and the soft ground is untested territory for him.

runners_data.name: Under The Twilight
runners_data.note: Won twice on good ground at 6f this term; hold-up runner from draw 1 who historically delivers a sustained finish on fast surfaces — Harry Davies can slot in rail-side early, though his lone soft start produced an eighth, which is a concern.

races.paceDynamic: Padua is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no rival likely to seriously press for the lead, should control the tempo from draw 5 on genuinely Good to Soft ground — a surface that rewards horses who can travel and cover ground without over-extending early. Behind him, Tenbob Tommy, Sergeant Pep, Baldomero and Safari Dream all want prominent positions, creating a congested group jostling for the first four spots from the off; the most likely flashpoint is 2-3f out when that cluster compresses into the final bend. Padua's ability to dictate a sustainable, uncontested gallop is the defining structural fact of this race — he won't be sprinting away, but he'll control fractions, which narrows the gaps for those coming from behind. This race shape most favours hold-up horses with a proven late kick on easy ground — specifically those comfortable sitting fourth to sixth and picking through traffic — though the prominent types in the slipstream of Padua remain dangerous if the pace is merely modest and they never fully clear their lungs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Padua Dictates, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Padua leads at a controlled gallop and the prominent congestion spends energy sorting positions, hold-up runners pounce in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Padua sets a comfortable tempo that stretches nothing, leaving hold-up horses fresh enough to deliver a sustained run from 2f out; the soft ground further compresses the field and rewards those who travel widest and latest.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pace Heats Up
scenarios.trigger: If Safari Dream or Tenbob Tommy chase Padua aggressively, the early tempo rises and prominent types in the slipstream steal the finish.
scenarios.body: A hotter early pace burns off the deeper hold-up horses and leaves the race to those who grabbed cover just off the leader in the first two furlongs; Sergeant Pep's soft-ground form and Rossa Ryan's positional instincts make him the natural beneficiary.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Caught In Traffic
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent cluster creates a wall 2-3 out and hold-up horses find no gap, the race is stolen by those who secured a clean outside run early.
scenarios.body: Horses forced wide find the better ground but lose ground, so only those with the raw ability to absorb the detour win through; Supreme King's recent Salisbury soft form gives him the engine for this, but the scenario hinges on clear sailing.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Padua Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground takes a heavier toll than expected and Padua's uncontested front-running proves far more potent than his rating suggests.
scenarios.body: A wire-to-wire result becomes possible if the pace is genuinely slow and hold-up horses simply cannot quicken on the dead surface; Padua's tongue-tie and Hughie Morrison's prep form support this as a low-probability but live outcome.

watchPoints.text: Prominent congestion warning — Tenbob Tommy, Sergeant Pep, Baldomero and Safari Dream all want positions 2-5, and the rush for those slots in the opening furlong could cause interference or force one or more wide, costing them the race.
Safari Dream (draw 9) may be forced to go hard from wide to secure a prominent pitch; if he chases Padua aggressively, the early pace rises and the entire race shape shifts away from Scenario A.
Supreme King's hold-up style from draw 8 leaves Pat Cosgrave dependent on a clear late run through a congested group — any traffic at the 2f pole could cost him the race regardless of ability.

The going is being called Good to Soft despite a Soft declaration in the race title; if the track has dried slightly from morning, horses with soft-going doubts (Under The Twilight, Supreme King) become more competitive.

Padua's soft-going form is poor, and if he struggles to maintain his natural gallop on the surface, the uncontested pace scenario collapses — watch his action in the early furlongs for any sign of labouring.

races.name: Happy 40th Birthday Kevin Baker Selling Stakes

runners_data.name: Persian Land
runners_data.note: Top-rated horse in the field at OR 75 with a recent win on soft going at six furlongs and a placed effort on soft at eight, travels mid-division which is the textbook profile for this pace shape; David Evans's yard is in form and Callum Rodriguez's booking is a positive.|

runners_data.name: Absolute Diamond
runners_data.note: Won last time out over this course's sister trip at seven furlongs on soft, handled the conditions well and Pat Cosgrave knows the track; OR 67 is workable and two recent placed soft-ground efforts confirm the going is no issue.|

runners_data.name: Hello You Ten
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with a "fades in finish" warning who will clash with Minzaal Time for the early lead, making it likely she burns out before the final furlong; her only form over seven furlongs was a sixth on good going which does not inspire.|

runners_data.name: Minzaal Time
runners_data.note: Shares the pace-setter role but has finished no higher than fifth in five starts, with a string of stamina races over seven furlongs at Sandown suggesting the trip is fine but the class barrier has been a consistent problem; blinkers applied.|

runners_data.name: Courage Best
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile with limited soft-going form — zero wins or places in five soft-or-similar runs — and the very short turnaround of four days since last run is worth monitoring; this race shape suits it on paper but the evidence of ability is thin.|

runners_data.name: Oxber Flyer
runners_data.note: Unknown quantity with no OR, no visible form figures and no going classification; trainer Charlie Clover has a modest two winners from four runners in the past 14 days and nothing in the profile anchors a strong view either way.|

runners_data.name: Our Fella
runners_data.note: Naturally prominent but carries the "fades in finish" flag and has been unable to win in eight career starts, with zero wins or places in similar going; the 7lb claimer for Isobelle Chalmers is notable and adds further uncertainty.|

runners_data.name: Lushill
runners_data.note: Scorecard danger with course-compatible form at seven furlongs and placed efforts over distances from six to eight furlongs; William Cox takes the ride for J S Moore and the draw at 10 is wide but neutral on this flat track, making gate position manageable.|

runners_data.name: The Kalonji Man
runners_data.note: A natural mid-division type whose OR of 45 is the lowest in the field and whose form figures — nothing above a fourth in nine starts — limit enthusiasm; placed at the rear of the redistribution list because there are more front-running and prominent types than positions.|

runners_data.name: Grapple

races.paceDynamic: Minzaal Time and Hello You Ten are confirmed front-runners and will battle for the early lead from stalls 5 and 2 respectively, creating a genuinely contested pace on soft ground over seven furlongs at Salisbury. Both carry the "fades in finish" tag, meaning their duel is likely to burn them out before the straight, setting up a proper end-to-end gallop that will test stamina thoroughly on this ground. Our Fella will press prominently from stall 6 alongside Lushill from the outside, adding further early pressure and ensuring no one gets a soft lead. This shape — contested up front, honest gallop, soft ground — strongly favours horses who travel mid-division with a turn of foot or prominent racers who can slot in just off the speed without over-committing early; The Kalonji Man has been redistributed to the rear because the field is stacked with front-running and prominent types, meaning Persian Land, Lushill and Our Fella are the ones most likely to actually secure meaningful early positions behind the pace-setters.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Closers Reel Them In
scenarios.trigger: If Minzaal Time and Hello You Ten burn each other out setting a genuine clip, the race falls apart for front-runners in the closing furlong.
scenarios.body: The contested duel scorches the early pace on soft ground, leaving the field strung out, and any runner with tactical cover mid-division who travels smoothly into the straight will find a wall of tired horses to pick off.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Endure
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is honest but not truly punishing, the better prominent types settle just behind and sustain their effort to the line.
scenarios.body: Lushill's experience over seven furlongs and Absolute Diamond's recent winning form on soft ground give them the fitness and class to hold their challenge through the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two leaders — most likely Hello You Ten — dictates a more measured gallop after the initial break and the field fails to press hard enough.
scenarios.body: A controlled gallop on going that is described on course as Good To Soft rather than heavy softens the stamina test, leaving residual pace for whichever leader settles better and avoids an all-out early war.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is truly fierce and the field comes back dramatically in the straight, opening the door for horses racing furthest back.
scenarios.body: Courage Best or Grapple, racing off a genuine end-to-end gallop, could pick up late, though Grapple's fade flag and Courage Best's limited form make this the least reliable outcome.

watchPoints.text: Watch Minzaal Time and Hello You Ten in the first two furlongs — if they genuinely tear into each other for the lead the race could be run at a breakneck pace that turns this into a thorough stamina test and dramatically inflates the chances of mid-division types like Persian Land.

Persian Land is unproven at seven furlongs having run exclusively at six and eight furlongs; if the extra furlong catches her out in the final stages on soft ground, Absolute Diamond — who won over this exact trip on soft — could move through as the stronger stayer.

Lushill's wide draw at stall 10 is not an automatic problem on a flat track but William Cox will need to decide early whether to push across for cover or ride the outsider's rail alone; a wide trip throughout on soft ground costs stamina.

Oxber Flyer is a complete unknown — no OR, no recent run date and an unknown-going tag mean any market move for this Charlie Clover runner in the ring should be treated as significant new information rather than noise.

The going board consistently shows Good To Soft for this 5:26 race despite the declared Soft; if the track is riding faster than expected that softens the stamina premium and marginally helps the front-running pair to sustain their efforts longer than the pace-dynamic analysis assumes.

races.paceDynamic: Three confirmed front-runners — Amiloc, Quickthorn, and Nightime Dancer — guarantee a strong, unrelenting gallop over 1m6f on soft ground at Salisbury, a flat course that nonetheless tests stamina thoroughly at this trip. Amiloc (OR 114, Ralph Beckett) and Quickthorn (OR 108, Hughie Morrison) are the classier pace-setters and will contest the early lead, with Nightime Dancer (OR 93) likely hustled along to hold a position that may prove unsustainable on this ground. The inevitable early friction and honest pace on soft turf will drain reserves from those in front, compressing the field and setting up a searching test that historically rewards a horse travelling powerfully off the pace who can strike decisively in the final two furlongs. This race shape decisively favours the hold-up or prominent-patient profile: specifically a horse that can sit off the contested lead, preserve energy through soft ground, and produce a sustained late run — making Lion's Pride, if his form returns after a 133-day absence, the primary threat to any front-runner who survives the war of attrition.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners burn each other out through a genuinely strong pace on soft ground, leaving a stamina-soaked final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: The early battle between Amiloc, Quickthorn, and Nightime Dancer creates a truly honest gallop that drains the leaders, turning the race into a stamina grind won by whoever best absorbs the pressure; a horse travelling smoothly off the pace with a strong staying pedigree finds the gaps opening. This is the dominant shape given the confirmed pace volume and soft conditions that exaggerate the cost of front-running.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Amiloc Controls and Stays
scenarios.trigger: If Amiloc establishes a comfortable lead without a sustained early war and dictates a measured gallop that suits his class advantage.
scenarios.body: As the highest-rated runner at OR 114 trained by Ralph Beckett and ridden by Rossa Ryan, Amiloc has the class ceiling to dictate terms if Quickthorn and Nightime Dancer settle behind rather than press him; on soft ground a controlled front-running display over 1m6f is viable for a horse of his ability. The Strand Scorecard identifies Amiloc as the top pick, and this scenario vindicates that read — class at the head of affairs proving decisive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses dramatically and Lion's Pride, returning from 133 days off, produces the expected strong late run for Gosden.
scenarios.body: Lion's Pride was a hold-up type who won over 12f on good ground and steps up markedly in trip here on soft, but the Gosden yard is in strong form (T14: 9/27) and Havlin is an astute partner for a patient ride; a truly strong pace on soft sets the table perfectly for a late challenge. The risk is the long absence and a trip and ground combination that is untested in his recent history.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Lottery
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground causes erratic performances, with front-runners stopping suddenly and no finisher producing a clean sustained challenge.
scenarios.body: In this low-probability chaos scenario, the three leaders tie each other up, soft ground catches out horses unproven at this trip and going combination, and the result is messy and hard to predict from pace analysis alone; Soul Icon, with prior soft-ground form, could scramble home if the race falls apart.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Amiloc or Quickthorn seizes the early lead — if Amiloc is pressed hard immediately by Quickthorn and Nightime Dancer, the pace will be genuinely suicidal on soft ground and the race is on for closers.

Lion's Pride's 133-day absence is a significant fitness question; if he moves freely in the early stages and Havlin settles him efficiently, he is the most dangerous horse in the race for the dominant pace scenario — watch his travelling position at halfway.

Nightime Dancer (OR 93, blinkers) may go off too fast in an attempt to hold a front position against OR 108 and OR 114 rivals; if he burns out by the home turn, his fading body could disrupt the race pattern for horses trying to progress.

Soul Icon's trip drop from 22-24f to 1m6f is worth monitoring — if she settles better than usual in mid-division rather than chasing the pace, the drop in distance could flatter her stamina-heavy profile on soft ground late on.

races.paceDynamic: Fanciulla Del West, Relentless Hero, Takeitorleaveit and Next Guilian all carry genuine front-running profiles into a 1m2f Salisbury handicap on soft ground, ensuring this will be run at a strong, unrelenting gallop from the outset with no scope for any one horse to dictate cheaply. That sustained pace over ten furlongs of soft turf will almost certainly turn this into a thorough stamina test in the final two furlongs, burning off those with fade warnings (Relentless Hero, Eljowhary) and exposing any hold-up horse who fails to get cover early. This field contains more front-running and prominent types than the pace map can accommodate — Takeitorleaveit holds the best claims to actually securing the lead given Portman's runner has the best recent form at the head of affairs, while Next Guilian and Fanciulla Del West are most likely to settle just off it rather than dominate. The resulting shape — strong pace, soft ground, genuine stamina emphasis — clearly favours horses who travel mid-division with a smooth cruising speed and finish powerfully late, or those prominent enough to save ground without burning out; in this field, Takeitorleaveit's proven ability to race positively and sustain it gives it the structural edge the Scorecard identifies.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace, Stayer Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the four front-runners burn each other off and the race becomes a searching stamina test in the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: The soft ground amplifies the attrition and horses who over-raced early — particularly Relentless Hero and Fanciulla Del West with fade warnings — will be swallowed up turning for home, leaving those who conserved energy in the first half free to assert. This shape rewards a horse like Takeitorleaveit who has the tactical speed to sit just off the boil and sustain an effort into the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace horses — most likely Takeitorleaveit — secures a clear lead and the rivals cancel each other out in a messy tactical battle.
scenarios.body: With multiple pace horses competing for the same real estate, the one that settles most comfortably without fighting for position could steal an uncontested lead by default as rivals check and jostle; Takeitorleaveit's recent form string of placed runs at the front suits this outcome precisely. If that horse clears the traffic and controls fractions slightly, soft ground notwithstanding, a prominent hold of the rail becomes decisive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace completely collapses in the final two furlongs and a true closer finds daylight to pick off the weary leaders.
scenarios.body: Soft ground occasionally produces a truly extreme burn-up that clears the path for late finishers, and Scarlet Letter or Sax Avoidance, racing from the back, could profit if that collapse is severe enough. However, Gatlinburg's redistribution to midfield means it is racing out of its natural hold-up role, discounting its ability to produce a genuine sustained late run — making this scenario thinner than it might appear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Type Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the race fragments into groups and a mid-division horse finds a clean passage at the two-furlong pole to pick up running horses.
scenarios.body: Miss Guinevere or Mid Flight could benefit if they settle centrally, avoid the early scrapping of the front-runners and produce a timed run as the leaders tire; both carry neutral draw positions that permit this line. The probability is constrained because soft ground at Salisbury tends to reward those who are positionally involved rather than those attempting a wide or through-the-gap finish.

watchPoints.text: Relentless Hero and Fanciulla Del West both carry fade-in-finish flags and will be racing against each other for the lead on soft ground — watch whether either burns out before the final two furlongs and collapses, which determines whether SCENARIO_A triggers.

Gatlinburg returns after 105 days and, as a true hold-up horse forced into an unnatural midfield position by the dominant pace, could give a misleading early impression — do not read its mid-race position as a positive tactical move.

Eljowhary's last two runs produced 10th-place finishes at 12f, and with a confirmed fade flag and soft ground at Salisbury, watch for an early exit from contention if the pace is strong from the outset.

Takeitorleaveit's ability to actually secure the lead unchallenged is the race's pivotal question — if Next Guilian or Fanciulla Del West push it into a duel through the first half-mile on soft ground, the pace tax on all three could open the door for Scarlet Letter or Sax Avoidance.

The going report consistently reads Good to Soft across all Salisbury races today despite the SOFT label in the race header — if the ground is riding faster than advertised, pace horses retain more residual energy and the lead scenario becomes correspondingly stronger.
